'''Allen Ivar Knutson''' is an American mathematician who is a professor of mathematics at [[Cornell University]].<ref>[https://math.cornell.edu/allen-knutson Faculty profile], Cornell University, accessed 2021-06-08.</ref>

== Education ==
Knutson graduated from Stuyvesant High School and completed his undergraduate studies at the [[California Institute of Technology]]<ref name="discover" /> and received a Ph.D. from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1996 under the joint advisorship of [[Victor Guillemin]] and [[Lisa Jeffrey]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|name=Allen Ivar Knutson|id=37047}}</ref>

== Career ==
He was on the faculty at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] before moving to the [[University of California, San Diego]] in 2005 and then to [[Cornell University]] in 2009.<ref>[http://math.ucsd.edu/about/department-history/ Department history] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190609032341/http://www.math.ucsd.edu/about/department-history/ |date=2019-06-09 }}, UCSD mathematics department, accessed 2012-06-20.</ref> In 2005, he and [[Terence Tao]] won the [[Levi L. Conant Prize]] of the [[American Mathematical Society]] for their paper "Honeycombs and Sums of Hermitian Matrices".<ref>[https://www.ams.org/notices/200504/comm-conant.pdf 2005 Conant Prize], AMS, accessed 2012-06-20.</ref> He was an invited speaker at the 2022 International Congress of Mathematicians.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vsnL0SWDNsI Schubert calculus and quiver varieties] half-hour YouTube lecture</ref>

Knutson is also known for his studies of the [[mathematics of juggling]].<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=38rf9FLhl-8 The mathematics of juggling] one-hour YouTube lecture</ref> For five years beginning in 1990, he and fellow Caltech student David Morton held a [[Juggling world records#Balls|world record]] for passing 12 balls.<ref name="discover">{{citation|title=The Mathematics of . . . Juggling: An algebra whiz reveals the secrets of keeping a lot of balls in the air|journal=[[Discover (magazine)|Discover]]|url=http://discovermagazine.com/2004/dec/mathematics-of-juggling|date=December 2004|first=Bill|last=Donahue}}.</ref>

== Personal life ==
Knutson is the son of Donald Ivar Knutson, an American mathematician and financial executive at [[CBS]].<ref name="a554">{{cite web | title=Paid Notice: Deaths<br>KNUTSON, DONALD I. | website=NYTimes.com | date=2018-04-02 | url=https://archive.nytimes.com/query.nytimes.com/gst/fullpage-9A04E1DD153AF937A25754C0A96F9C8B63.html }}</ref>
